decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - The proposed vehicle crossover would be consistent with the Supplementary Planning Guidance. The location and design of it would not harm the safe and free flow of traffic along the street, or the movement of pedestrians and vehicles into and out of the site. The presence of yellow lines at the front of the site would ensure that no on-street car parking spaces would be lost. The proposed boundary treatment and landscaping would also protect the appearance and character of the street. The proposal is consistent with the Supplementary Planning Guidance and consistent with adopted Unitary Development Plan policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development), T.4.4 (Road Safety), T.4.5 (On-street parking) and T.5.3 (Vehicle Crossovers and Hardstandings).
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of five years from the date of this permission.
Condition : 3 - The proposed vehicle crossover must not be constructed wider than 2.4m at the front boundary of the site.

Condition : 4 - A splay of 2.4m x 2.4m shall be provided on each side of the access, the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, and no fence, wall or other obstruction to visibility exceeding 0.6m in height above the surface of the adjoining highway shall be erected within the areas of such splays.
Condition : 5 - The boundary wall as shown in the site plan, shall be reinstated within two weeks of completion of the vehicle crossover.
Condition : 6 - The hereby permitted crossover should be provided with a 4.8m gap between this crossover and the existing crossover at no.72 Martindale Road.
Condition : 7 - The proposed forecourt landscaping shall be carried out before the vehicular access is first brought into use and thereafter retained permanently
description: Creation of vehicular access to front of house.
